title: How Long After Breast Augmentation Can I Swim? Pool, Ocean
meta_description: At least about a month, and until incisions are fully closed and your surgeon agrees. Pool, ocean, hot tub and how to protect new scars.
excerpt: Pools, the ocean and hot tubs all wait at least about a month, and until your incisions are fully closed and your surgeon agrees. Here is what the sources say about each kind of water, when a bathing suit is fine, why laps come later, and how to protect new scars from the Florida sun.
quick_answer:
How long after breast augmentation can I swim?

At least about a month, and until your incisions are fully closed and your surgeon agrees, an article on the ASPS website and UW Medicine say. It is often quoted as 4 to 6 weeks, but that range comes from a UW Health handout on breast reconstruction. UW Medicine allows showers after 48 hours.

quotes: Do not take a bath, sit in a hot tub, or go swimming until your incisions are fully healed.

Wash very gently and use mild soap on your incisions or over your Steri-Strips.
Keep the Steri-Strips on until they fall off. Remove them after 2 weeks if they are still on.
Your doctor will decide if you need a surgical bra. If you are given one, keep it on 24 hours a day for 3 to 4 weeks. Take it off only when you shower.
Do not wear an underwire bra until your incisions are fully healed.

After three to four weeks of wearing the surgical bra, you can transition into a soft, supportive sports bra.

You will begin to notice your final results around three months after surgery. However, you may continue to have subtle changes throughout the 12 months following your surgery.
